about: volteridentity's decision table (the P3 procedure): Volter Identity's OpenID Connect provider, device grant, social sign-in and product organizations API as the in-scope products call them (journeys/demand.json). Every served operation is a handler; the derived core serves none (no operation of the spec is plain CRUD on a resource the pack declares). Every other operation answers the gap.

decisions.demand: Twin, Volter Harness, Substrate, Open Autonomy and RH2: each reads the discovery document first
decisions.why: computed: the captured discovery document's fields (spec/recordings), EdDSA as the vendor advertises

decisions.demand: every product's browser sign-in (Twin, Volter Harness, Substrate, Open Autonomy, RH2)
decisions.why: an action over a session: the client and its redirect checked (loopback on any port), PKCE required of a public client, prompt=login and no session to the sign-in page, else a code kept by its SHA-256 and the redirect with code, state and iss

decisions.demand: every product's code exchange; Twin's client_credentials token; Volter Harness's and Substrate's refresh for a resource; Volter Harness's and RH2's device polling; shared-client predecessor reuse and ordinary device recovery
decisions.why: an action: client authentication (basic, post, or a public client by id), the authorization_code (PKCE S256), refresh_token and client_credentials grants and the device code; held-resource and scope checks precede revoked reuse, current resource linkage is checked only for active issuance; signed tokens; only actual refresh successor issuance rotates a predecessor, while a grant without offline scope remains reusable; apply the pinned provider's zero-grace same-client/person reuse invalidation, then allow a normal fresh device grant; no thirty-second replay claim

decisions.demand: Twin, Volter Harness, Substrate and RH2 read the email and name the ID token keeps out
decisions.why: computed from the access token: the person's claims for its scopes and their linked GitHub account

decisions.demand: Twin, Volter Harness's Teams server, Substrate, Open Autonomy and RH2 verify tokens against the issuer's keys
decisions.why: computed: the World's signing key as a JWKS

decisions.demand: Volter Harness (the shared public client) and RH2's desktop widget (confidential, with its secret)
decisions.why: an action: the client authenticated, a device code and a user code kept until approved or expired

decisions.demand: RH2's iOS app claims the console's device code with its session
decisions.why: an action over a session: a pending, unclaimed code claimed by the signed-in person; its status, and its client and scope for the claimant

decisions.demand: RH2's iOS app approves the code it claimed
decisions.why: an action over a session: only the claimant approves a pending code; refusals in Better Auth's device errors

decisions.demand: RH2 iOS Apple ID-token request (apps/rh2-mobile/apple.ts:41); hosted GitHub/Google sign-in (identity worker/ui/identity.ts:126)
decisions.why: an action: the provider's ID token verified against its keys at the World's twin of the provider (issuer, audience, age, nonce raw or SHA-256), the person found, linked or made, a session cookie; without an ID token the provider's authorize URL

decisions.demand: The hosted identity page uses configured GitHub/Google sign-in; their callbacks exchange codes through the provider twins and link the account before product authorization
decisions.why: an action: the provider's code traded at the World's twin of the provider, the person found or linked, the session set, back to the authorization request

decisions.demand: Twin's directory finds a person by email
decisions.why: a gated read: the product's organizations token; the person by email or 404

decisions.demand: Twin's directory reads a person
decisions.why: a gated read: the person by id or 404

decisions.demand: Twin's directory reads a person's organizations of this product
decisions.why: a gated read: the person's memberships in the product's organizations, each with the role

decisions.demand: Twin creates an organization
decisions.why: a gated action: the slug checked and unique, the organization owned by the product, its creator the owner member

decisions.demand: Twin reads an organization by id or slug
decisions.why: a gated read: only the product's own organizations

decisions.demand: Twin renames an organization
decisions.why: a gated write: the name only, the slug kept

decisions.demand: Twin deletes an organization
decisions.why: a gated delete: its members removed with it

decisions.demand: Twin lists an organization's members
decisions.why: a gated read: members with the person's email and name

decisions.demand: Twin adds a member
decisions.why: a gated action: a Volter identity, admin or member, not twice

decisions.demand: Twin changes a member's role
decisions.why: a gated write: owner, admin or member

sourceRules.means: role is owner, admin or member

decisions.demand: Twin removes a member
decisions.why: a gated delete

decisions.demand: Twin invites by email
decisions.why: a gated action: an invitation for a week, admin or member, from a Volter identity

decisions.demand: Twin lists pending invitations
decisions.why: a gated read: pending and unexpired

decisions.demand: Twin revokes a pending invitation
decisions.why: a gated state move: pending to canceled

decisions.demand: every product's people
decisions.why: Existing emailed-code or passkey identities are created outside the served API; linked social accounts are made only by social sign-in and its provider callback.

decisions.demand: the sign-in page's GitHub and Google; RH2's iOS app's Apple
decisions.why: the service's OAuth apps at the providers and the iOS apps Apple signs in are the operator's configuration (GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, APPLE_APP_IDS)

decisions.demand: the operator registers Open Autonomy's giving page and Twin's console (world.ts:68, rehearsal.ts:32), and every product the life signs in
decisions.why: an action behind a signed-in session and the admin token: Better Auth's client metadata checked and defaulted, a client id and (confidential) secret minted from the World's secrets, the secret answered once and kept by its SHA-256

decisions.demand: the resources Substrate's gateway and Volter Harness's tokenFor name (volter.ts:240, shared.js:359) exist once the operator registers them
decisions.why: an action behind the session and the admin token: an https origin or the organizations door, once

decisions.demand: Twin's console linked to <issuer>/organizations (rehearsal.ts:38); the gateway and the shared client linked to theirs
decisions.why: an action behind the session and the admin token: the token endpoint answers a resource only for a client linked to it

decisions.demand: Volter Harness's @volter/identity signs in with the shared client its package names
decisions.why: the operator's API mints a client's id; only a door makes the client under the id @volter/identity publishes (SHARED_CLIENTS)

decisions.demand: the operator's admin token for the World's application that registers products
decisions.why: IDENTITY_ADMIN_TOKEN is the operator's setting, which no API reads; the descriptor's credentialDoor hands it to the application under that name

decisions.demand: the World's own door, POST /_twin/settings: the service's permanent ISSUER binding, configured before OAuth account setup; defaults to its declared id.volter.ai host
decisions.why: The service's permanent ISSUER binding, configured before OAuth account setup; defaults to its declared id.volter.ai host, which no vendor API makes.
